nodes.name: Pulsed Laser Deposition and RTA
nodes.procedure: The confined NiFe NPs catalysts were prepared on glassy carbon electrode substrates by PLD technique combined with a RTA process. First, the permalloy (NiFe) (99.9%) and carbon (99.9%) targets were alternately ablated by KrF pulsed laser (248 nm) under ultra-high vacuum conditions ≈ 5×10^{-8} Torr. The laser energy was 300 mJ and the frequency was 10 Hz with a pulse width of 10 ns. During the deposition, both NiFe/carbon target and substrate rotated slowly around their central axis. After 5 min of PLD deposition, the NiFe NPs composites were rapidly thermal annealed at 400°C for 5 min under Ar atmosphere at 100 sccm.

nodes.name: In situ Electrochemical Reconstruction
nodes.procedure: The synthesis of NiFe/NiFeOOH core/shell NPs was achieved by EC-reconstruction based on PLD-prepared confined NiFe NPs on glassy carbon electrode. This was conducted by using the three-electrode system of CHI 760E electrochemical workstation with NiFe NPs as working electrode, saturated Hg/HgO as reference electrode, and graphite rod as counter electrode. The in situ EC-reconstruction was performed with cyclic voltammetry (CV) at 50 mV s⁻¹ for 40 cycles from 1.0 to 1.8 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) in 1.0 M KOH electrolyte.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-density NiFe NPs with average diameter of ≈9 nm and spherical nanostructures are confined in amorphous carbon matrix.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2a, the typical low-resolution TEM (LRTEM) image implies that high-density NiFe NPs with a good homogeneity were successfully confined in an amorphous carbon matrix. These monodispersed NiFe NPs present spherical nanostructures with an average diameter of ≈9 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern matches cubic NiFe structure with space group Fm3m.
nodes.evidence_snippet: By matching the simulated electron diffraction pattern produced by TEM Java electron microscopy simulation (JEMS) software with the corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of NiFe NPs (Figure 2b), it can be concluded that the crystal structure of the NiFe NPs is a cubic structure with a space group of Fm3m.

nodes.characterization_summary: Single crystallinity NiFe NP displays lattice spacing of 0.18 nm corresponding to (200) plane of cubic NiFe alloy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2c shows the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image of a representative single NiFe NP, displaying a single crystallinity with lattice spacing of 0.18 nm, which can be related to the crystallographic (200) plane of cubic NiFe alloy.

properties.description: TEM image showing circular particle with 0.18 nm marking, scale bar 6 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: All XRD patterns indexed to permalloy with cubic structure (JCPDS No. 47-1417).
nodes.evidence_snippet: All of the XRD pattern in Figure S1, Supporting Information, can be indexed to a permalloy with cubic structure (JCPDS No. 47-1417), in agreement with the TEM results.

nodes.characterization_summary: Homogeneous distribution of Ni, Fe, and C elements with Ni:Fe content ratio of 1:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S2, Supporting Information, the homogeneous distribution of Ni, Fe, and C elements in the PLD-prepared NiFe NPs indicated the compact confined nanostructure and the Ni:Fe content ratio was measured as 1:1.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p peaks at 869.9 and 852.7 eV (Ni⁰) and Fe 2p peaks at 719.8 and 706.6 eV (Fe⁰) confirm metallic nature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Ni 2p region (Figure S3a, Supporting Information), the doublet peaks located at 869.9 and 852.7 eV can be assigned to Ni⁰ 2p₁/₂ and Ni⁰ 2p₃/₂, respectively. The additional doublet peaks located at 719.8 and 706.6 eV in the Fe 2p region (Figure S3b, Supporting Information), correspond to the Fe⁰ 2p₁/₂ and Fe⁰ 2p₃/₂, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Room-temperature superparamagnetism shown by s-like M-H curve without coercivity at 300 K.
nodes.evidence_snippet: And an s-like hysteresis without coercivity was observed in the magnetization versus magnetic field (M-H) curve at 300 K (Figure 2d), indicating the room-temperature superparamagnetism of NiFe NPs.

properties.description: Magnetization vs Field at 300K, M in 10^0 emu, H from -0.25 to 0.25 T

nodes.characterization_summary: Core/shell nanostructured NPs observed with average size of 11 nm after EC-reconstruction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2e shows the representative low-resolution TEM (LRTEM) image of the reconstructed NPs, in which the core/shell nanostructured NPs are clearly observed. And the average size of NPs after EC-reconstruction is about 11 nm.

properties.description: Transmission Electron Microscopy image showing nanostructure with labeled distances

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern matches cubic NiFe core structure after reconstruction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2f shows the corresponding SAED pattern of the core/shell NPs. The SAED pattern matches well with simulated electron diffraction pattern of cubic NiFe NPs, indicating the retention of NiFe core in the reconstructed NPs.

properties.description: High-resolution TEM or diffraction pattern with rings and peaks

nodes.characterization_summary: Core/shell NP shows highly crystalline core and 1.52 nm amorphous shell with 0.18 nm lattice spacing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the HRTEM image in Figure 2g shows a typical core/shell NP, displaying a highly crystalline core and an ultra-thin (about 1.52 nm) amorphous shell. The lattice stripes of the core exhibit the same 0.18 nm plane spacing as previous NiFe NPs.

properties.description: TEM image of nanoparticle with 0.18 nm and 1.62 nm markings, scale bar 6 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: No obvious differences in diffraction pattern from NiFe NPs, indicating amorphous NiFeOOH shell.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S7, Supporting Information, no obvious differences in the diffraction pattern are observed between the reconstructed core/shell NPs with the NiFe NPs, suggesting the amorphous feature of the formed NiFe-derived (oxy)hydroxides shell.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p peaks at 856.4/874.2 eV (Ni³⁺), Fe 2p at 712.5/725.6 eV (Fe³⁺), O 1s at 529.4/531.2/533.0 eV confirm NiFeOOH shell.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p region (Figure S8a, Supporting Information), shows two doublet peaks located at 856.4 and 874.2 eV, which can be assigned to Ni 2p₃/₂ and Ni 2p₁/₂ of Ni³⁺. The Fe 2p region (Figure S8b, Supporting Information), presents two peaks at 712.5 and 725.6 eV... The three peaks located at 529.4, 531.2 and 533.0 eV in the O 1s region (Figure S8c, Supporting Information), can be attributed to the typical metal-oxygen bonds, oxygen in the hydroxide group and chemisorbed molecular water, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Superparamagnetic behavior at 300 K with s-like M-H curve without coercivity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The 300 K s-like M-H behavior without coercivity behavior in Figure 2h indicates that NiFe/NiFeOOH core/shell NPs is superparamagnetic.

nodes.characterization_summary: After 16 h OER operation, morphology and lattice structure of NiFe/NiFeOOH core/shell NP unchanged.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The representative HRTEM image of a single NiFe/NiFeOOH core/shell NPs after long-term electrochemical operation clearly shows that the morphology and lattice structure have not changed (as shown in Figure 5b).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern after long-term operation matches cubic NiFe alloy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 5c shows the SAED pattern, which is well matched the simulated electron diffraction pattern of cubic NiFe alloy.

nodes.characterization_summary: After 16 h durability test, XPS peaks show no significant shift or change in intensity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 5d–f shows the spectrum of NiFe/NiFeOOH core/shell NPs after the 16 h durability test. The XPS results show that the XPS peaks do not show a significant shift and change in intensity.

nodes.characterization_summary: No detectable Fe or Ni leaching into electrolyte after long-term operation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In stark contrast to the two distinct peaks located at 259.941 and 231.604 nm... the ICP-AES characterization of our electrolyte after long-term operation exhibits undistinguished signal at the corresponding wavelength.
